title: Alibaba Soars 6% as Apple Sets December Launch for Qwen-Powered iPhone AI in China
summary: Apple sets December launch for Qwen-powered iPhone AI features in China
detailed: Alibaba shares rose 6% following Apple's announcement that Apple Intelligence will launch in China in December using Alibaba's Qwen model.
The deal helps offset recent financial losses in Alibaba's AI Labs and Applications segment by lowering customer acquisition costs via Siri integration.
Alibaba traded at 12x forward earnings with negative free cash flow in five of the last six quarters.
sentences: Alibaba ( BABA ) is up 6% today after Apple ( AAPL ) said Saturday that Apple Intelligence will launch in China in December, built on Alibaba’s Qwen model.
Some of the jump is policy: JD.com ( JD ) and PDD Holdings ( PDD ) rose too, on reports Chinese regulators met with banks and brokerages to support the market.
The deal helps with the bill: Alibaba’s AI Labs and Applications segment lost RMB 13.9 billion (adjusted EBITA) in the June quarter, partly from marketing the Qwen app.
A Qwen button inside Siri wins users far more cheaply.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from RMB 26.80 per ADS in fiscal 2026 (years to March) back to about fiscal 2024’s level by fiscal 2028:
For Apple, the launch closes a feature gap with Huawei .
Its Greater China sales rose 30% to $64.8 billion in the nine months to June 27 without Apple Intelligence.
Apple, down 1%, reports after today’s close, and I’ll be listening for its China outlook.
JD.com and PDD get nothing from Apple’s deal, so their gains are all policy.
They traded at 7.1x and 6.9x forward earnings at the last close, but neither is growing much: JD’s revenue fell 2.9% in the June quarter, and PDD’s online marketing revenue grew 3%.
I’d want to see sales pick up in their November reports before buying the rally.

Alibaba traded at 12x forward earnings at the last close, a touch under its five-year average of 13x and about half its January peak:
At today’s price, it’s right around that average.

That’s a full price for a company with free cash flow negative in five of the last six quarters, including a RMB 44.7 billion outflow in the June quarter:
I think today’s jump is deserved, but the stock needs its late-November report to show the AI Labs loss shrinking.
Of course, the new Siri isn’t in the first wave, so we won’t know for a while how many iPhone users reach for Qwen.
